instruction.text: You’re talking to a historian about the fire. Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: How long did the fire ((dance ++burn)) for?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-0.5st'>How long did the fire burn for?</prosody>

atoms.b: The fire burned through London for around ((++4_days 30_days)).
How did the people of ((Sydney ++London)) react?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-0.5st'>How did the people of London react?</prosody>

atoms.b: Many people helped to put out the fire. Other people escaped on ((++boats trains)) down the river.
Did anybody ((++write garden)) about this event?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-0.5st'>Did anybody write about this event?</prosody>

atoms.b: Yes! We have the diary of Samuel Pepys, who ((++wrote ate)) about the fire and how people dealt with it.
atoms.sound: Yes! We have the diary of Samyul Peeps, who wrote about the fire and how people dealt with it.

atoms.b: He famously wrote about burying his expensive ((phone ++cheese)) to prevent it from burning!
atoms.sound: He famously wrote about burying his expensive cheese to prevent it from burning!

instruction.text: Match each description of how the fire spread to the correct image.

atoms.b: Buildings were close together, so the fire travelled quickly.
Strong winds blew the fire from building to building.
Buildings caught fire easily after a hot, dry summer in London

instruction.text: Select the horses to find out how people were putting out the fire.

feedback.end: People used horse-drawn carts to take water from the River Thames up to the burning buildings. There were no fire engines back then!
